syllabusTopics: Gaseous state: Kinetic theory of gas and its postulates
Gas laws: Boyle's law, Charles' law, Avogadro's law, combined gas equation, Dalton's law of partial pressure, Graham's law of diffusion
Ideal gas and ideal gas equation; universal gas constant and its significance
Deviation of real gas from ideality (solving related numerical problems based on gas laws)
Liquid state: physical properties of liquids — evaporation and condensation, vapour pressure and boiling point, surface tension and viscosity (qualitative idea only)
Solid state: types of solids, amorphous and crystalline solids
Efflorescent, deliquescent and hygroscopic solids; crystallization and crystal growth; water of crystallization
Introduction to unit crystal lattice and unit cell

card.title: The Gaseous State — Characteristics and Measurable Properties

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The kinetic molecular theory rebuilds a whole gas from five sentences: molecules are **tiny points** in vast empty space, flying **randomly** in straight lines, feeling **no forces** between collisions, bouncing **perfectly elastically**, and carrying **average kinetic energy proportional to absolute temperature** — the same for every gas.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - PV = ⅓ nMu²(rms) - u(rms) = √(3RT/M); u(av) = √(8RT/πM); u(mp) = √(2RT/M) - KE per molecule = 3/2 kT; per mole = 3/2 RT - u(rms) ratio for two gases = √(M₂/M₁)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **"Elastic" collisions conserve energy — they do not stop motion:** a common answer loses marks by saying molecules "come to rest" after collisions.  ·  **Speeds are a distribution, not a single value:** u(mp), u(av), u(rms) describe one Maxwell–Boltzmann population; quoting one formula for "the speed" is imprecise.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "The average kinetic energy of gas molecules is directly proportional to the absolute temperature and is independent of the nature of the gas."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Perfume across a room*** — no fan, yet the scent arrives: random molecular flight at hundreds of m/s plus countless collisions spreads it — diffusion as postulate 2 in action.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQ: NEB 2024 — postulates of the kinetic molecular theory (solved above). Other items are NEB-style practice.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Why Gases Are the Simplest State Solids have shape, liquids have surface, gases have **nothing but motion**. The kinetic molecular theory explains every gas law from five postulates about point particles in random flight — and it succeeds because gas molecules are so far apart that they barely interact. This topic supplies the model; the next topics supply its equations.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 The five postulates (NEB 2024 verified list) 1. **Tiny particles:** gases consist of a very large number of molecules, tiny compared with the distances between them — the molecular volume is negligible against the container volume. 2.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Postulate mnemonic: "Tiny, Random, Free, Elastic, KE–T". Speed ladder: "most probable < average < RMS". Ratio u(rms) gases = √(M₂/M₁).

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB 2024 (4m): Write the postulates of the kinetic molecular theory of gases.** — The kinetic molecular theory describes a gas by five postulates: **(1)** A gas consists of a very large number of tiny particles (molecules) whose actual volume is negligible compared with the volume of the container — most of a gas is empty space.…  ·  **NEB-style (2m): Calculate the ratio of the root mean square speeds of hydrogen and oxygen molecules at the same temperature.** — From the kinetic gas equation, u(rms) = √(3RT/M), so at the same temperature u(rms) ∝ 1/√M. For H₂ (M = 2) and O₂ (M = 32): ratio = √(32/2) = √16 = **4 : 1**.…

rows.text: Number the postulates 1–5 and keep each to one sentence — examiners tick them individually. Adding the consequence line (explains gas laws; defines ideal gas) earns the synthesis mark.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: The kinetic model is the bridge between the gas laws (topics 44–45) and real-gas deviation (topic 46): every deviation is one of the five idealisations failing.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Five postulates: negligible molecular volume; random straight-line motion with collisions; negligible intermolecular forces; perfectly elastic collisions; average KE ∝ absolute T (same for all gases at a T). Pressure = wall-collision momentum transfer; PV = ⅓nMu²(rms).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: The interstellar medium is a kinetic-theory laboratory: hydrogen atoms at 10⁶ K in nebulae move at ~10 km/s, and the same √(3RT/M) arithmetic sizes stellar winds.

rows.text: **NEB-style (2m): Explain why a gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container according to the kinetic theory.** — Gas molecules move randomly at high speeds and collide with the walls (postulate 2).…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ## 6. Common Confusions **Elastic does not mean "bouncy" in the everyday sense:** elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy — the gas does not cool as its molecules collide, which is why a sealed bottle stays at room temperature.  ·  **Same KE, different speeds:** at 25 °C helium and oxygen molecules have the same average kinetic energy; helium simply moves ~2.8× faster (√(32/4)) — students conflate energy with speed.  ·  **RMS, not average, enters the equations:** the kinetic gas equation uses u(rms) because pressure depends on the mean of v², not the mean of v.
